---
title: "Equivalent reporting-loss scales"
subtitle: "5.2 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), Section II"
description: "Affine equivalence of KRW's loss and postrank's risk over the six-site report family."
---

The complete six-site family contains 4,683 coherent reports. Each is evaluated under KRW's loss at reward λ and
postrank's risk at the corresponding withholding cost τ. The scatter compares these two evaluations and identifies
their minimising sets. Under the stated tie-free and common-family conditions, an increasing affine transformation
relates the objectives, so their optimal reports coincide. The grid check repeats this comparison across cost
settings. An additional archived firm card is evaluated as a fixed report and retains the distinction between its
original selection probabilities and the released evaluation probabilities.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **λ 1, flat line** gives slope 0. The full order 1/2/3/4/5/6 has DR .0480 and expected correct minus wrong per pair .904. KRW call these minimising grades Condorcet ranks. The separate 97-firm grid card is evaluated as a fixed report.
- **λ .25** gives slope 3. Both objectives choose 1/2/3/3/4/5, with postrank risk .0372. The ring marks a coherent report, rather than a collection of independent pair decisions.
- **τ .25, whole grid** checks every report at every one of 49 τ settings. The two complete minimising sets agree at 49 of 49 values. The table gives the corresponding decimal λ and complete grade vectors for both objectives.
- **λ .08** gives τ .0741 and 1/1/2/2/3/3. More pairs share a grade when a correct direction earns less.
- **τ .40** moves the other slider: λ becomes 2/3 and the full order returns. Arrow keys on the figure read every report, including reports away from the best line.

The correspondence requires a tie-free target and the same posterior probabilities, orientation, units and report family. For every such report, postrank's risk at τ equals τ plus one minus τ times KRW's risk at the matching λ. The reported residual checks this identity over the complete family; it measures floating-point rounding, not posterior calibration. Equal-risk tolerances determine which reports remain in each minimising set.

The additional KRW card uses released probabilities for evaluation, while KRW's code chose it under archived probabilities. It is not claimed to be optimal here.
